hyperedges.label: One-time certificate custody and delivery flow

nodes.label: Flujo por API / HEADLESS (F1, §16)
nodes.rationale: Chosen F1 2026-10-22; no provider frontend, no webhook; ally drives TyC, request, Civil Registry, FaceLiveness, issuance.

nodes.label: Async job chains (Tramo A/B/C via Bus::chain)
nodes.norm_label: async job chains (tramo a/b/c via bus::chain)
nodes.rationale: Flow can't be one chain because human liveness interaction sits between steps; IssueCertificate Tries(1) never retried blindly.

nodes.label: Capability contracts (SignatureProvider, RegistersRequests, QueriesStatus, HandlesWebhooks...)
nodes.rationale: Not all providers offer all flows, so a driver implements only the capabilities it has.

nodes.label: CertificateVault (aes-256-gcm, VAULT_KEY)
nodes.rationale: Separate vault key distinct from APP_KEY protects against APP_KEY theft; password encrypted with a further key.

nodes.label: Data model (api_clients, tenants, provider_accounts, signature_requests, certificate_vault, webhook_events, usage_ledger, client_notifications, audit_logs)
nodes.norm_label: data model (api_clients, tenants, provider_accounts, signature_requests, certificate_vault, webhook_events, usage_ledger, client_notifications, audit_logs)
nodes.rationale: Biometric data and documents are forwarded, not persisted (LOPDP minimization).

nodes.label: Evidence package (EvidenceLog, EvidencePackageBuilder, EvidenceEncryptor, CMS)
nodes.rationale: Chained presign/sign makes modifying, deleting or reordering events break the chain.

nodes.label: FaceLiveness temporary AWS credentials (encrypted cache, Cache::pull once)
nodes.norm_label: faceliveness temporary aws credentials (encrypted cache, cache::pull once)

nodes.label: FirmaSeguraHttpClient
nodes.rationale: No retry() on POST: idempotency comes from referenceTransaction and 409.

nodes.label: Linked Partner (Tercero Vinculado) flow (F3, §15)
nodes.rationale: Ally validates identity and sends signed evidence; certificate issued immediately but requires own identity verification component (largest risk).

nodes.label: Permission / Role spatie enums (->value rule)
nodes.rationale: spatie/laravel-permission only recognizes BackedEnum, so spatie enum classes always pass ->value.

nodes.label: ProductType (internal products: REGULAR, TRANSACTIONAL, LINKED_PARTNER, SIMPLIFIED, HEADLESS, POS_VOUCHER)
nodes.norm_label: producttype (internal products: regular, transactional, linked_partner, simplified, headless, pos_voucher)
nodes.rationale: SaaS speaks in provider-independent products; each driver translates to the concrete provider flow.

nodes.label: ProviderWebhookController (verify -> TX -> 200 -> job)
nodes.rationale: Webhook is never sole source of truth; state changes without certificate are confirmed with status().

nodes.label: SignatureProviderManager (Illuminate Manager)
nodes.rationale: Same Manager pattern as Mail/Cache/Filesystem; switching provider = register new driver, SaaS unchanged.

nodes.label: UsageGuard (hard caps)
nodes.rationale: Hard caps in the gateway independent of SaaS quotas, with Cache::lock per tenant, LimitExceeded event and alert.

nodes.label: UUIDv7 on all models (HasUuids, uuidMorphs for Sanctum/permission)
nodes.norm_label: uuidv7 on all models (hasuuids, uuidmorphs for sanctum/permission)

nodes.label: gateway:* Artisan commands (keys:generate, provider:credentials, tenant:create, client:create)
nodes.norm_label: gateway:* artisan commands (keys:generate, provider:credentials, tenant:create, client:create)

nodes.label: ApiClient tenant-scoped auth (Sanctum token + HMAC, TenantScope)
nodes.norm_label: apiclient tenant-scoped auth (sanctum token + hmac, tenantscope)
nodes.rationale: Token alone is bearer; HMAC binds each request to body and time so captured requests can't be replayed. Tenant deduced from token limits blast radius.

nodes.label: Layered data protection (13 layers: field encryption, vault, blind index...)
nodes.norm_label: layered data protection (13 layers: field encryption, vault, blind index...)
nodes.rationale: Full-DB encryption at rest does not protect against app compromise or SQL injection, so layers are used.

nodes.label: Topology: WireGuard internal API + public webhook surface
nodes.norm_label: topology: wireguard internal api + public webhook surface
nodes.rationale: Two separate HTTP surfaces: internal API only on tunnel interface, public webhook restricted to provider IPs; provider token lives only in gateway, IP-restricted.

nodes.label: Domain vs provider-specific enums (app/Signing/Drivers/FirmaSegura/Enums)
nodes.rationale: Provider enums translated by driver mapper so a second provider does not pollute the domain.

nodes.label: Sealed one-time certificate delivery (sodium_crypto_box_seal, DeliveryMode)
nodes.rationale: Delivery mode derived from product: HOLDER when provider sends p12 directly, CLIENT_SEALED when p12 reaches gateway; only SaaS can open.
